commonMistakes: Do not say active transport “moves water”. Water movement across partially permeable membranes is osmosis.
A partly correct response can still miss a required form, unit, relationship or mark point.
detailedExplanation: Active transport is needed when a cell must accumulate a substance even though there is already more of that substance inside the cell than outside. This cannot happen by diffusion alone.

Examples: - Root hair cells absorb mineral ions from very dilute soil solutions. - Cells in the small intestine can absorb glucose even when glucose concentration in the gut is lower than in the blood.
